procedure: Take a liquid in which the given solid does not dissolve.
Note the initial position of liquid surface.
Put the solid in the cylinder containing liquid.
Note again the position of liquid surface in the cylinder which rises due to solid.
Find the volume of the solid by subtracting the initial reading from the final reading.
aim: To find the volume of a solid by measuring the rise in liquid level in a graduated cylinder.

viva.question: How is the volume of the solid found?
viva.answer: By subtracting the initial liquid reading from the reading after immersing the solid.

viva.question: Why must the liquid not dissolve the solid?
viva.answer: Dissolving would change the solid and make its volume measurement inaccurate.

viva.question: How should you position your eye when taking a reading?
viva.answer: Keep the eye in front and in line with the lower meniscus.

viva.question: What causes the liquid level to rise?
What is the SI unit of volume?
How many cubic centimetres are in one millilitre?
viva.answer: One millilitre equals one cubic centimetre.

apparatus: Liquid in which the solid does not dissolve
diagram: Draw two graduated cylinders: label the initial liquid level A in the first cylinder; in the second, draw the solid immersed in liquid and label the higher liquid level B, and label both cylinders and the liquid.
title: Volume of a solid by liquid displacement
precautions: Use a liquid in which the solid does not dissolve.
Keep your eye in front and in line with the lower meniscus while taking each reading.
Put the solid gently into the cylinder to avoid splashing liquid.
Ensure the solid is completely immersed and has no air bubbles attached to it.
result: The volume of the solid is 18 mL, or 18 cm³.
